title: Federal Reserve Signals Cautious Approach to Rate Cuts as US Inflation Remains Above Target
text:
The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee held the federal funds rate target range at 5.25 to 5.50 percent at its September meeting, maintaining the highest policy rate level in over two decades. Chair Jerome Powell emphasized that while progress on inflation has been meaningful, the committee needs greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward the two percent objective before beginning a rate-cutting cycle.

The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures price index showed core PCE inflation at 2.6 percent on a year-over-year basis, down from 4.8 percent at its peak but still above the Fed's symmetric target. Shelter costs continue to exert upward pressure, contributing approximately 60 percent of the remaining inflation overshoot, while goods deflation has largely run its course. Labor market conditions have cooled gradually, with nonfarm payroll gains averaging 150,000 per month over the past quarter and the unemployment rate edging up to 4.2 percent.

Fed officials' September dot plot projections indicated a median expectation of two 25-basis-point rate cuts in 2024, down from three cuts projected in June. Several regional Fed presidents, including those from Dallas and Cleveland, have publicly advocated for patience, citing risks that premature easing could re-ignite inflationary pressures. Financial markets have responded with increased volatility in the two-year Treasury yield, which serves as a key barometer of near-term rate expectations.

Looking ahead, the Fed's dual mandate framework will weigh employment gains against price stability. Economists at major Wall Street institutions forecast the first rate cut in November or December 2024, contingent on two consecutive months of core PCE readings at or below 2.5 percent. The Fed's balance sheet normalization program continues on autopilot, with monthly Treasury runoff capped at $25 billion, adding an additional layer of quantitative tightening to the policy mix.
